articles.title: Two Seminyak Villas Went Fully Booked on the Same Day. It Was Day 180
articles.excerpt: I run a visa agency in Bali, which means I spend a lot of time looking at how full the island is. One of the Apify Actors I maintain reads Airbnb's availability calendar — the grid you see when you op…
articles.body: I run a visa agency in Bali, which means I spend a lot of time looking at how full the island is. One of the Apify Actors I maintain reads Airbnb's availability calendar — the grid you see when you open the date picker on a listing — and returns it as rows: free nights, taken nights, the host's minimum stay per date, occupancy per month, up to twelve months ahead. Yesterday I pointed it at my own neighbourhood. Twenty listings, a full year, everything on: { "locationQueries" : [ "Seminyak, Bali, Indonesia" ], "maxListings" : 20 , "calendarMonths" : 12 , "includeDays" : true } 22.9 seconds, 20 rows, $0.05 for the lot. The calendars run from 2026-10-30 to 2027-09-30 — 336 nights each, 6,720 nights in total. Mean occupancy across the twenty: 33.9%.

articles.title: Giving AI Coding Agents a Memory That Argues Back
articles.excerpt: I'm writing a series called "Becoming a Super Engineer": a software engineer since 2013, learning to hold software, data and AI under the same belt, and writing it down as it happens. Chapter 1 ended…
articles.body: I'm writing a series called "Becoming a Super Engineer": a software engineer since 2013, learning to hold software, data and AI under the same belt, and writing it down as it happens. Chapter 1 ended with agents that only stopped repeating mistakes once a check failed on them. This chapter is about the other half of that problem: what agents remember. It's about an open-source project of mine, a knowledge base the agents read before touching anything and write back to when they're done. It taught me a lot about working with agents :) Two agents without memory, two different correct APIs. The one with memory gave back the fix we had recorded The problem: every session starts from zero Without persistent memory, an AI coding agent forgets everything between sessions.

articles.title: Squado - Your engineering org on one live canvas
articles.excerpt: I am an engineering manager and the thing I could never keep current was not the code, it was the shape of the org. Who sits where, what each team is carrying, what it costs. That lived across a sprea…
articles.body: I am an engineering manager and the thing I could never keep current was not the code, it was the shape of the org. Who sits where, what each team is carrying, what it costs. That lived across a spreadsheet, a wiki page and some Slack threads, and it was stale the moment I finished assembling it. Squado is one canvas with alliances, tribes and squads and the people on them. Drag someone into another squad and pick whether they transfer or stay on both. Vacation, split allocations and open seats show on the faces. Set hourly rates by role once and cost rolls up per squad, tribe and alliance. OKRs attach to the squads that own them, and the ceremony calendar flags the overlaps. The link goes straight into a fictional fintech org, 10 squads and the people on them, no signup and no account.

articles.title: I let my coding agent do the whole localization job, from messy keys to approved translations
articles.excerpt: Every app I ship exists on iOS and Android, some on the web too. After a few releases the half of them hard-coded in SwiftUI views and Compose screens the rest in Localizable.xcstrings under keys like…
articles.body: Every app I ship exists on iOS and Android, some on the web too. After a few releases the strings were a mess: half of them hard-coded in SwiftUI views and Compose screens the rest in Localizable.xcstrings under keys like "Sign in" , account.login and login_button , all for the same button the Android app with its own names for everything ( R.string.login_btn ) the web app with a third set ( auth.signIn ) Three names for one text means three translations, three chances to drift, and nobody knows which one is right. What I wanted Say "localize this app" to my coding agent, and get it done properly : not a quick translation that breaks a placeholder or puts a German sentence into a toolbar button.

articles.title: The Worst GTA Game Is One Rockstar Could Never Make Today
articles.excerpt: GTA Advance might be one of the worst GTA games, but it was still an essential stepping stone for what makes GTA great today
articles.body: GTA Advance is an odd game. It's terrible in some ways, yet also not as bad as its reputation suggests. It's also an essential part of Rockstar history. This was Rockstar at a stage of uncertainty. The essence of the Grand Theft Auto franchise was still in flux, and the studio had yet to firmly decide on what, exactly, made a GTA game . GTA Advance has its strong points, but the most important thing about it is how it gave Rockstar (via developer Digital Eclipse) a chance to see where the series could fall short. It's a necessary bad game that paved the way for better ones — and the kind of essential failure the games industry can't tolerate anymore.

articles.excerpt: After five days of living underwater, Analog Astronaut Commander Dr. Musilova and her crew return to terra firma, affected by higher pressures and the team's disconnection from home.
articles.body: Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. On one hand, you are excited to return to your home and loved ones, as well as to fresh food and normal hygiene. On the other, you know you will miss your crew and the incredible experience of being in space. While my SEA STAR crew and I had not left Earth during our mission, we were separated from the surface of our home planet for five days. All we saw was a green alien water world surrounding us. We did this to live and work like astronauts on the ISS .

articles.excerpt: India launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite to orbit today (Oct. 30) atop a GSLV rocket. It was the fourth orbital launch from Indian soil so far this year.
articles.body: India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30). A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. (Image credit: ISRO) NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System ( GPS ).

articles.body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Someone has created a tool called UnknownAuto that lets self-built or sideloaded apps run on Android Auto. The tool marks the app as “installed from Google Play,” so Android Auto accepts it. UnknownAuto is billed as a free, open-source alternative to AA Enabler. Android Auto can run a large variety of apps, but not every app. The platform refuses to run apps that have been sideloaded. If there was ever an app you wished could run on Android Auto but doesn’t, there may be a solution. One user, who goes by u/mannumaster on Reddit, says they wanted to build their own app and use it on Android Auto. When they ran into roadblocks, they created a new tool called UnknownAuto. This tool is free, open-sourced, and can work offline.

articles.body: TL;DR Some YouTube users are reporting a bug that randomly kicks videos out of full-screen mode and into the floating mini player. The glitch also kills audio playback, forcing users to restart videos or the YouTube app to restore sound. Common troubleshooting steps haven’t helped. We’ve contacted Google to ask whether a fix is in the works. Despite its never-ending battle against ad blockers , YouTube otherwise offers a mostly fuss-free video streaming experience, especially if you’re a Premium subscriber. You open the app, scroll and find something you want to watch, and hit play. But what if even that seamless experience starts showing signs of instability? That’s precisely what some YouTube users, on both Android and iOS, are experiencing right now.
